item.title: FIFA Executives Were Given Ultimatum to Approve World Cup Privatization Plan
item.description: The day before the World Cup final, key FIFA figures faced a stunning demand to sign off on a multibillion-dollar privatization project.
item.dc:creator: Tariq Panja
item.media:description: Spain’s players celebrate winning the World Cup. UEFA, European soccer’s governing body, led the opposition to the plan.

item.title: Amid Cyclospora Outbreak, Demand for Locally Grown Lettuce Surges
item.description: Small produce stands and farmers’ markets are seeing a surge in demand for leafy greens as sales of lettuce and salad kits from grocery chains and big retailers drop.
item.dc:creator: Julie Creswell
item.category: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
item.media:credit: Amir Hamja for The New York Times
item.media:description: Lettuce at a farmers’ market in New York City this week. Sales of prepackaged salads in grocery and other retailers dropped in July, as the confirmed cases of cyclospora grew.

item.title: Drought Threatens a Vital Economic Artery in the Heart of Europe
item.description: The Rhine conveys vessels and cargo that power European industry. Record low water levels are disrupting supply chains, adding costs and presenting fresh risks to growth.
item.dc:creator: Christopher F. Schuetze, Patricia Cohen and Patrick Junker
item.media:description: The wreck of a fishing boat that sunk in 1996 is one of several long-submerged relics exposed by low water levels.

item.title: China’s Unitree Prices IPO in Bet Investors Are Ready for Humanoid Robots
item.description: Unitree Robotics wants to raise about $900 million in an I.P.O. that tests market interest in humanoid robots, a technology that wows but has yet to prove its viability.
item.dc:creator: Steve Lohr and Xinyun Wu

item.title: The ‘Heated Rivalry’ Star Hudson Williams Uplifts a Canadian Tire Bag
item.description: After the actor Hudson Williams was photographed carrying a plaid reusable shopping bag, priced under $2, the tote has become a viral fashion accessory.
item.dc:creator: Vjosa Isai
item.media:description: Hudson Williams, who plays the gay hockey player Shane Hollander in “Heated Rivalry,” at the Golden Globes in January.

item.title: What’s Behind the A.I. Shake-Up at Google
item.description: A new role for Demis Hassabis, the head of Google’s artificial intelligence unit, reflects reality at the tech giant. Investors remain worried.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe and Sri Muppidi
item.media:credit: Pool photo by Julia Demaree Nikhinson
item.media:description: Demis Hassabis, center, with President Trump and President Lee Jae Myung of South Korea. He leads artificial intelligence at Google but acts as more of a statesman for the technology.

item.title: Follow the Markets and Track Stocks With These Free Apps
item.description: Google Finance and Apple’s Stocks app have added new features over the years to make them more useful for tracking the markets and your investments.
item.dc:creator: J. D. Biersdorfer
item.media:description: Apple's free Stocks app for its devices provides a dashboard for following personal investments, markets and financial news.

item.title: Why So Many C.E.O.s Are Getting a Chief of Staff
item.description: The position as a trusted sounding board is in high demand as business gets more complex — and everyone wants to get in on the latest bureaucratic fad.
item.dc:creator: Jordyn Holman
item.media:credit: Oliver Farshi for The New York Times
item.media:description: Richard Gelfond, IMAX’s chief executive, and Natalie Mayer, his chief of staff. His various chiefs of staff, he said, have helped him “think through what I want to say and what I want to accomplish and then how to execute it.”

item.title: F.D.A. Approves Moderna’s mRNA Flu Vaccine
item.description: The agency had initially refused to even review the application but reversed course after a public outcry.
item.dc:creator: Christina Jewett
item.media:description: Moderna has said that the faster new approach used to prepare the vaccine will enable a shift away from the current process of focusing on one flu strain for an entire hemisphere each season and allow each nation to pick its best option.

item.title: TikTok Lays Off 250 Employees in Office That Includes Content Moderation
item.description: TikTok did not give a detailed reason for the layoffs, which will shutter its Nashville office.
item.dc:creator: Emmett Lindner
item.media:description: In January, TikTok’s Chinese parent company, ByteDance, spun out an American venture to operate in the United States.

item.title: Bessent Declares Widening Gap Between Rich and Poor ‘Dead’
item.description: Despite data to the contrary, the Treasury Secretary made the case that the K-shaped economy no longer exists.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport
item.media:description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent during a hearing on Capitol Hill in June. He said Tuesday that “the K-shaped economy is over.”

item.title: Bunny Dolls and Disturbing Allegations: Max Miller’s Strange CNN Interview
item.description: In a 23-minute appearance with the anchor Jake Tapper, the Ohio Republican made an unusual effort to rebut a multitude of allegations that have threatened his re-election bid.
item.dc:creator: Michael M. Grynbaum
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Max Miller was interviewed live on CNN about his allegations on Tuesday.

item.title: Pilot Smuggled 55 Pounds of Ecstasy Into Indonesia, Officials Say
item.description: The pilot, identified only by his initials, also tested positive for ecstasy and cocaine when he was arrested last week at the Jakarta airport, the Indonesian police said.
item.dc:creator: Johnny Diaz
item.media:credit: Soekarno-Hatta Airport Customs, via Agence France-Presse

item.title: What the Stock Market’s Record Rally Has to Do With Rescuing the Yen
item.description: The wide impact of the U.S. intervention into the Japanese currency shows the extent to which global markets’ revolve around investments in artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Joe Rennison
item.media:description: The Treasury Department intervention into the Japanese yen highlighted the interconnected nature of global markets.

item.title: Four Top Google A.I. Researchers Form New Start-Up
item.description: Jeff Dean, who for years was one of Google’s most important executives, is leading the new artificial intelligence company with the backing of Google.

item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: Quoc V. Le, left, Oriol Vinyals, Jeff Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat are leaving Google to start a new A.I. company called Discovery Loop.

item.title: The Winners of Trump’s A.I. Safety Plan

item.title: The New York Times’s Revenue Rises 11% as Costs Increase

item.dc:creator: Katie Robertson
item.media:description: The New York Times Company said it had 13.35 million total subscribers at the end of the second quarter.

item.title: Disney Theme Parks Report Strong Results, While Comcast’s Universal Parks Dip
item.description: Theme parks have long been seen as a bellwether for consumer confidence. Disney’s domestic parks and cruises revenue rose 11 percent in the latest quarter.
item.dc:creator: Brooks Barnes
item.category: Disney, Walt, World (Lake Buena Vista, Fla)
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: Sleeping Beauty Castle at Disneyland Park in Anaheim, Calif. Attendance at the company’s parks in Florida and California rose 3 percent for the quarter.

item.title: Disney+ Cracks Open the Door to TikTok Creator Videos
item.description: Disney said it would allow “thoughtfully curated” fan-created videos, using clips from its library, to appear on the streaming service.
item.dc:creator: Brooks Barnes
item.media:credit: Wolf von Dewitz/picture alliance, via Getty Images
item.media:description: The new collaboration is meant to give people a reason to open Disney+ even when they don’t have a specific movie or show in mind.

item.title: Wildfire Smoke and Airport Chaos: My Summer Vacation From Hell

item.title: Chipotle Removes Jalapeños Linked to Salmonella Outbreak From Its Restaurants
item.description: The Minnesota Department of Health said it had identified 110 salmonella cases in this outbreak, and the F.D.A. is also investigating.
item.dc:creator: Alena Cerro

item.media:description: Chipotle said it “proactively removed the jalapeños from our restaurants and replaced them with product from different growers.”

item.media:description: Portraits of President Trump and Vice President Vance hang in the employee entrance of the Environmental Protection Agency in Washington.

item.title: Judge Sets Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Trial for March
item.description: Paramount, which struck a $111 billion deal to acquire Warner Bros., had requested a November trial for an antitrust lawsuit brought by state attorneys general.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Mullin

item.media:description: A trial is scheduled to determine whether Paramount’s purchase of Warner Bros. violates an antitrust law.

item.title: SpaceX, in First Earnings After IPO, Reports Soaring AI Spending
item.description: Elon Musk’s rocket company said its capital expenditures jumped nearly seven times from a year ago. Revenue also rose.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac
item.media:credit: Karsten Moran for The New York Times
item.media:description: In its first earnings report as a public company, SpaceX also posted a quarterly loss of $541 million, narrower than the $1 billion loss in the same period a year ago.

item.title: Justice Dept. Charges Doctor in $95 Million Skin Substitute Fraud Scheme
item.description: Dr. Stephen Dubin, a wound care doctor in Nevada, is accused of applying unneeded, expensive wound coverings to seniors. He used the profits to buy yachts, the department said.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Kliff
item.media:description: The Justice Department said that Dr. Stephen Dubin used his Medicare earnings to finance a lavish lifestyle.

item.title: S&P 500 Hits Record High as Stock Market Worries About Iran and AI Ease

item.title: Man’s Claim That Brakes Failed on Jaguar Was Scam to Avoid Car Payments, Court Rules

item.dc:creator: Victor Mather

item.title: Medicaid Urges States to Increase Autism Therapy Oversight
item.description: The program’s spending on the therapy has quintupled since 2021, far outstripping the growth in diagnoses and raising concerns about overprescribing and fraud.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Kliff
item.media:description: An autism therapy clinic in North Carolina in April. The state is on track to spend $1 billion on autism therapy next year, compared with $121 million in 2022.

item.title: Why Wall Street Is Feeling So Bullish

item.title: A SpaceX Rocket Will Soon Crash Into the Moon
item.description: The second stage of a Falcon 9 rocket, which sent two private landers to the moon last year, will collide with the moon early Wednesday morning.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chang
item.media:description: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket carrying two private lunar landers launched in January last year. The second stage of this rocket will hit the moon at 5,400 miles per hour on Wednesday.

item.title: These New Travel Initiatives Could Slash Airport Wait Times
item.description: U.S. airlines and airports are experimenting with initiatives that screen passengers and their bags more efficiently in an effort to slash wait times.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chung

item.title: Pacific Palisades Shopping Center Set to Reopen Following Palisades Fire
item.description: Rick Caruso, the billionaire real estate developer and former Los Angeles mayoral candidate, is reviving a property still surrounded by burned-out lots.
item.dc:creator: Kim Bhasin and Shawn Hubler
item.media:credit: Ariana Drehsler for The New York Times
item.media:description: Palisades Village mall, which was largely intact after the devastating Los Angeles wildfire last year, is nearly complete and set to reopen Aug. 15.

item.title: Inside Uber’s Legal Strategy to Fight Sexual Assault Lawsuits
item.description: Our investigative reporter Emily Steel reviewed about a dozen lawsuits against Uber by riders who say they were sexually assaulted or harassed during their rides. They reveal the aggressive tactics Uber’s lawyers are taking as part of their defense strategy.
item.dc:creator: Emily Steel, Christina Shaman, June Kim, James Surdam and Lauren Pruitt

item.title: Uber’s Strategy for Fighting Sexual Assault Suits: ‘What Were You Wearing?’
item.description: The ride-hailing giant promised to handle legal claims “in a way that is best for the survivor.” Its lawyers are pursuing a far more aggressive strategy.
item.dc:creator: Emily Steel

item.title: Sailors Working in Strait of Hormuz Are Caught in Crossfire of Iran War

item.media:credit: Tomas Munita for The New York Times

item.title: How the Mohegan Tribe Lost a Billion-Dollar Casino in South Korea

item.title: Education Dept. to Wipe Out Student Loans of 170,000 More Defrauded Borrowers
item.description: The sprawling case, centered on students defrauded by for-profit schools, has now become the largest class-action settlement in American history.

item.media:description: Kaplan College was one of the more than 150 institutions, mostly for-profit colleges, named in the 2022 settlement in the case.

item.title: Republicans Let Trump Keep Unparalleled Benefit: I.R.S. Immunity

item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren
